reports.title: Woodward Reports Record Sales & Earnings for Fiscal Year 2026

guidance.heading: Fiscal Year 2027 Guidance
section: Our fiscal 2027 guidance assumes a sustained strong demand environment, which will drive continued sales growth and margin expansion. As reflected in our guidance, margin rate expansion will moderate in fiscal 2027 due to higher investments in our manufacturing capabilities and capacity to ensure we can continue to increase production volumes, improve our structural cost position, and deliver durable earnings growth.

desk.headline: Sales up 17% to $1.16bn, beat; fiscal 2027 EPS outlook of $10.20–10.70 below estimates
results: Sales rose 17% to $1.16bn and adjusted EPS jumped 35% to $2.83, ahead of the $2.52 analysts expected; GAAP EPS was $2.74.
Aerospace grew 18% on commercial engine parts (+26%) and repairs (+25%), but defence services fell 12%; the segment margin held at 24.3%.
Industrial sales rose 14% and its margin jumped to 20.7% from 14.6%, helped by power generation (+18%).
Record year: sales up 22% to $4.36bn and adjusted EPS up 42% to $9.78.
Free cash flow fell to $131m as capital spending tripled to $163m; $154m went on buybacks in the quarter ($711m for the year), and debt rose to $1.42bn.

guidance.summary: First outlook for fiscal 2027: sales up 6–10% and adjusted EPS of $10.20–10.70, with free cash flow of $400–450m. Woodward says margin gains will slow as it invests in factories, and the end of China on-highway sales costs about $110m of sales.

points: Commercial aerospace demand stays strong: higher aircraft build rates, and every repair line grew in Q4; newer LEAP and GTF engine repairs now outsell older engines.
Aerospace margins are expected to be flat to slightly up in 2027 as about 150 bps goes into factory moves and productivity projects.
Industrial growth is held to 1–5% by the China on-highway wind-down; data-centre power demand tilts sales towards new equipment rather than service.
Defence aftermarket is lumpy; management sees openings in high-volume munitions and unmanned vehicles.
Interest costs are set to rise to about $75m on higher debt; shares fell about 1.7% after hours on the softer EPS outlook.
call.source: Call coverage: GuruFocus and Investing.com, 18 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: Whether margin expansion stalls as factory and capacity spending ramps up.
